content:
#1 nForum uses Vanilla 1.1.10. The development of Vanilla 1 stopped in 2012. Vanilla 1 was superseded by Vanilla 2, which was actively developed for a while, but the development was formally stopped at the end of 2025.

Modern LLMs automate the process of finding vulnerabilities and constructing exploits for them. I think we can confidently say that a software that wasn’t updated since 2012 is probably full of bugs and vulnerabilities. I suspect it is only a matter of time before a malicious entity exploits these vulnerabilities to break into nForum.

What options do we have to preserve the content of nForum’s database? For the content of the nLab itself, at least we have a git repository https://github.com/ncatlab/nlab-content. Can we make a similar repository for the nForum database? Or perhaps some other form of backup?

Otherwise we risk losing almost 20 years of history in the event of a hack.
subject: The security of nForum's database

content: #2 At least the server that runs the nLab software is being backed up, for whatever that’s worth.
subject: The security of nForum's database
